questions.q: Why does local state become a real problem once a second engineer needs to run terraform apply?
options: Terraform CLI can only be installed on one machine per company
The state file only exists on one machine, so no one else has a reliable, current copy of it
Local state files are always corrupted after one use
Azure blocks terraform apply from running on more than one laptop
questions.explain: A local terraform.tfstate file lives only on whichever machine ran apply last. A second engineer running from a different clone has no guarantee their copy matches reality.

questions.q: In the azurerm backend configuration, what does the storage_account_name attribute point to?
options: The storage account that holds the actual application data being provisioned
The Azure Storage Account where the state file itself is stored as a blob
A virtual machine's boot disk
The subscription ID
questions.explain: The azurerm backend stores the state file as a blob inside a dedicated Azure Storage Account and container, provisioned specifically to hold state.

questions.q: What do the bucket and key attributes identify in an s3 backend configuration?
options: The AWS account's billing settings
The S3 bucket and the specific object path where this configuration's state file is stored
A list of IAM users allowed to run Terraform
The EC2 instance type to provision
questions.explain: bucket names the S3 bucket and key names the exact object path within it, together identifying exactly where the remote state file lives.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed as a benefit remote state gives a team, according to the lesson?
options: Shared -- everyone reads and writes the same file
Durable -- survives any one laptop being lost or wiped
Automatically writes your entire .tf configuration for you
Lockable -- can prevent two applies from running at once
questions.explain: Remote state does not write your configuration for you. It provides a shared, durable, and lockable location for the state file -- configuration authoring is still your job.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail use two different backend types across its infrastructure?
options: Because the s3 backend doesn't actually work
Because Northbridge runs infrastructure on both Azure and AWS, and each cloud has its own natural backend choice
Because Terraform requires a different backend for every resource type
Because azurerm backends are being deprecated
questions.explain: Northbridge Retail is modernizing infrastructure on both Azure and AWS, so it uses an azurerm backend for Azure state and an s3 backend for AWS state.
